## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 5, titled *Aññacetāpana* ("Exchanging for something else"), is an analytical rule belonging to the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that if a nun receives one item through an attendant or steward but subsequently has it exchanged for something else, the item must be relinquished and the offense confessed [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Direct parallels within the Pali tradition include its corresponding rule in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-np5*) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Nissaggiya Pācittiya 5 [SuttaCentral]. Curated resembling parallels are recognized across several early Buddhist monastic codes under the designation *Aññaviññāpana* ("Requesting something else"), with versions preserved in Chinese and Tibetan translations of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates extensive formulaic overlap within the Pali Vinaya, sharing its longest textual sequences with adjacent Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules, especially Nissaggiya Pācittiya 4 (sharing 3,935 characters) and Nissaggiya Pācittiya 6 [DharmaNexus]. Across corpora, DharmaNexus identifies textual alignments with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) and commentary literature such as the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104) [DharmaNexus].
